Done. The root cause was that MCP tool discovery could only ever be run by an admin: `discoveryUserId` was set exclusively in the OAuth callback when `role === 'admin'`, so on a project where no admin ever connected the server, no tool specs were written to `agent/mcps/<server>/` and the agent genuinely had nothing to read — hence "I don't know any endpoint".

What I changed:

**A regular user now claims discovery when nobody owns it.** In the OAuth callback (`apps/backend/src/routes/mcp-oauth.ts`), an admin still always takes over discovery on connect, but any other member claims it when the server has no discovery owner yet, and their token is then used to list the tools. The new `claimMcpDiscoveryUser` query does the claim-if-unowned atomically so a user can never steal discovery from an admin.

**Users can trigger the first discovery themselves.** `mcp.discoverServer` moved from admin-only to `canSendProcedure`: admins can rediscover any time, everyone else only for a server that has no known tools yet (checked by the new `mcpService.hasDiscoveredTools`, which treats a failed discovery as undiscovered rather than trusting the empty spec folder on disk). Viewers are still excluded, and `discover` (Connect all) stays admin-only.

**The settings UI actually lets them do it.** Non-admins previously saw a dead "OAuth required" badge; they now get the same Connect button (the token is per-user anyway, and they could already connect from the chat prompt), plus the per-server refresh button while the server has zero tools. The MCP Servers page is also no longer hidden from non-admin settings search.

**The agent stops claiming the server has no tools.** The system prompt now says an empty server folder means discovery hasn't run yet and to ask the user to connect it from Settings → Project → MCP Servers, and the "OAuth connection required" status no longer says "an admin must connect this server".

Lint, format check and the backend MCP tests pass; I added a test covering `hasDiscoveredTools` distinguishing a failed discovery from a real tool list. The remaining lint warnings are pre-existing in unrelated files.
